newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope deplores killings of priests in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Pope deplores killings of priests in Rwanda.

text.p: Pope John Paul on Tuesday deplored the killing of six people, including two priests, in Rwanda.
The Vatican said Secretary of State Cardinal Angelo Sodano had sent a telegram in the Pope's name to the Bishop of Butare expressing the Pontiff's condolences over the killings.
Rwanda state radio said the six were killed in a bus in the south of the country by unidentified attackers on Sunday night in Gikongoro province.
The Vatican telegram said the Pope was shaken by the killings and identified the priests as Isaie Habakurama and Pascal Yirirwahandi.
It said they were victims of "unjustifiable attacks".
Rwandan radio said last week that 25 people were killed in Gikongoro between April 28 and 30 by unidentified attackers.
Rwandan Hutu rebels massacred 17 schoolgirls and a Belgian nun and wounded 14 other schoolgirls in an attack on schools in north-western Rwanda on April 29, state radio also reported.

Rwandan authorities say the attacks are mounted by former Hutu troops and Interahamwe militiamen who returned to Rwanda from Tanzania and Zaire with refugees late last year and who led the genocide of 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates in 1994.
